faq.q: Can I match the grade points to my own university?
faq.a: Yes. Under 'Edit grade → point mapping' you can change what each letter grade is worth on the selected scale (10-point India, 4-point US or percentage-based), add grades, or reset to default. The mapping is saved in your browser. When entering subjects you can type a letter that uses this mapping, or type a numeric grade point directly.

faq.q: How is the CGPA actually computed?
faq.a: It's a credit-weighted average, not a plain average of grade points. Each subject's grade point is multiplied by its credits, those are summed, and divided by total credits. The working box shows the full sum. This is why a weak grade in a five-credit core subject moves your CGPA far more than a strong grade in a one-credit lab.

faq.q: Which percentage conversion does it use?
faq.a: The CGPA → Percentage tool shows several at once — CBSE's CGPA × 9.5, CGPA × 10, and the AICTE-style (CGPA − 0.75) × 10 — plus any custom multiplier you enter, so you can match your institution. The tool warns that formulas vary by university and the only authoritative source is your institution's own regulations or conversion certificate.

faq.q: What does the Target CGPA calculator tell me?
faq.a: Enter your current CGPA, completed credits, target CGPA and remaining credits, and it computes the SGPA you'd need across the remaining semester(s) using (target×(completed+remaining) − current×completed) ÷ remaining. It flags the goal as not achievable if the required SGPA exceeds your scale's maximum, or already achieved if your current CGPA is above target.
